items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Roy Eldridge and Chu Berry and joined John Fletcher, and, of course, there was quite a story behind that, you know. John Fletcher was broadcasting...

ctx.x: Well, he recently was in Denver here at the Warehouse with the great Ella Fitzgerald, and I think he came in as an extra added attraction because he plays solos (soul, whatnot, and -- but there's a guy, I feel like I've always been closer to him, more than quite a few musicians because I remember Roy when I first had my band in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Roy is from a little town out of Pittsburgh called Duquesne, which the great Earl Hines came from. And Roy came in one day to the Hotel where we were stopping…

And he says, 'Hey man, I'm a trumpet player, can I sit in?' you know, one of those kind of things. And I looked at him, man; he had his little raggedy coat on, all this kind of stuff. I said, 'look at this cat.' You should have seen the horn. The horn was really raggedy. The bell was about half as big as it should have been, and the middle valve was off. That's -- this is what intrigued me. The little cap on it, you know, the little screw, that was off.
